anglicized_name: Manikula Phalca, translation: the phalcā of the jewel clan
description_en: Situated in the Kvaylāchi, Maṇikula Phalcā stands on the western side of the Sthāna Gaṇeśa temple of Kvaylāchi, on the street which leads from Kvaylāchi (south) to Cyāsal (north). The Phalcā was dismantled and rebuilt around 1995, incorporating four baluster columns which had been salvaged from an unknown location and shortened. Maṇikula Phalcā was commissioned by the Śākya of Maṇikūṭavihāra, which was established in 1865 as a branch of Cikã Bahī (LAL1620).Translated as "the Phalcā of the jewel clan", Maṇikula Phalcā has a very unusual, almost triangular ground plan. The three-bayed Phalcā´s ground shape is trapezial due to its location between the Gaṇeśa temple in the east and another building to the west.
description_ne: यो फल्चा क्वय्लाछि टोलमा अवस्थित छ । यसै टोलमा रहेको स्थान गणेशको मन्दिरको पश्चिमपट्टि, च्यासलबाट दक्षिणतिर क्वलायछि जाने बाटोमा यो फल्चा रहेको छ । तीन वटा कवल भएको यो फल्चा गणेश मन्दिर र एउटा व्यक्तिगत घरको बीचमा च्यापिएर रहेको छ । सन् १९९५ सालतिर यो फल्चा भत्काएर पुनर्निर्माण गरिएको थियो । कतै अन्यत्र राखिएको काष्ठस्तम्भ यसमा प्रवेश गरिएको थियो ।

Namaskār. Salutation to venerable Ganeśa. 9-22.  Bhikṣu Maṇiratna Vaidya and his wife Indralakṣmī, husband and wife who live in Nepal Maṇḍala in Lalitpur Mahānagara at Cyāsala Tole in Saptapuri Mahāvihāra, after originating dharmacitta (religious feeling) they have renovated this shrine of thrice venerable Ganeśa, Lord of the area, [and also] after making a golden icon of Ganeśa [and] also organizing Mangalbār Seva khalak (Tuesday Service Group of Gaṇeśa) [and] making a gold plated pinnacle, they have established [all of them in the temple] on the 4th day of the dark half of the Lunar month of Jeṣṭha in [NS] 982 (1862 CE).  And, wishing their dead son, daughter, grandson [and] granddaughters may get an abode in Sukhāvati heaven. [They] have arranged naivedya (food) to worship the deity and bhajan (recitation of the religious songs) every year on Indrajātrā in the dharmaśāla which was donated by them. In order to renovate the dharmaśālā , the donor Bhikṣu Maṇiratna has offered 5 ropanis of land named Thacheṣelaṣetra on 13th day of bright half of the lunar month of Bhadra in [NS] 983 (1863 CE). After performing such activities, the descendants of the donor may consume rest of the income (of the land). From this virtue, the donors may get dharma, fulfillment of their desires, prosperity, long life, fame, pleasure, health, money and children in this life and after this life (after their death) they may get to abode in Sukhavati, heaven. Maniratna, Indralakṣmī. May all be well. _ dā Malanasiṃ Rāj Datta, Munithakuṃ, Hiralakṣmī, Lānimunī, Cijamatī, Ratnakumārī (other family members).

historical_events.event_description: The inscription states that Bhikṣu Maṇiratna Vaidya and his wife Indralakṣmī commissioned the Phalcā in the hope that their descendants “may get an abode in Sukhāvati heaven”.

It is likely that the Phalcā got the name Maṇikula Phalcā ('the Phalcā of the jewel clan') because it belonged to a man called Maniratna of Maṇikula Bahā. The donor offered 5ropanisof land (called Thacheṣelakṣetra) to finance the renovation of the Phalcā. The descendants of the donors were allowed to use any surplus money.Donation of land, 5ropanīs
The Lalitpur sub-metropolitan city office donated funds (reportedly 1,40 thousand rupees) and land (totalling 5ropanis)for the reconstruction of the Phalcā.
